items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: Well, Henry Martin, the drummer I was telling you about, he used to work with Peter Bocas.

ctx.x: Well, would they have the bands in the houses or the cribs or the cabarets or what?

No, they were in cabarets. Yeah, you had Pete Lawless at Rice Cafe, you had Tom Anderson. And Lula White, she just had a piano player. And Tom Anderson. And Pete Barrett, they didn't have no band. And there was about four or five places around there that had bands working. Well, Henry Martin, the drummer I was telling you about, he used to work with Peter Bocas. Peter Bocas. Was it Peter Bocas? I think it was Peter Bocas. I used to work with Peter Bocas at the Rice Cafe. And that's at the corner of Iberville and…

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: Oh, it's a bright fella that played trumpet from downtown. His name was Pete. Creole Serenators.

ctx.x: Now, you were sick yourself around about this time, weren't you?

Yeah, I was. Yeah, I was sick. But not, you know, like I am now, you know? I was getting around, but it was pretty tough. But anyway... I'll give Larry credit... For starting off this jazz revival. Not, uh, not starting it off, but keeping it going. Because he took in, uh, I don't know what this place, what the hall was before he... Put the bands in there. But they tell me that punch...
